'''Nigel David Goldenfeld''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS}} (born May 1, 1957) is a Professor of Physics at the [[University of California, San Diego]].<ref name=gs>{{Google scholar id}}</ref> Previously he worked at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]], where he served as director of the [[NASA]] Astrobiology Institute for Universal Biology,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://astrobiology.illinois.edu/ |title="NASA Astrobiology Institute for Universal Biology" |access-date=2016-03-23 |archive-date=2016-04-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160402030713/http://astrobiology.illinois.edu/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> and the leader of the Biocomplexity group at [[Carl R. Woese Institute for Genomic Biology]].{{fact|date=May 2024}} 

==Education==
Goldenfeld was educated at the [[University of Cambridge]] (UK) where received his Ph.D. in 1982.

==Career and research==
Goldenfeld is a co-founder of [[Numerix]] and the author of the 1993 textbook "Lectures on Phase Transitions and the Renormalization Group,"<ref>{{cite web|author=Lawrie, Ian D.|title=Review of ''Lectures on Phase Transitions and the Renormalization Group'' by Nigel Goldenfeld|url=https://guava.physics.uiuc.edu/news/articles/Review_LPTRG.pdf}}</ref> a widely used graduate textbook in statistical physics. 

He is a Fellow of [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] and a [[Fellow]] of [[American Physical Society]] since 1995<ref>{{cite web|title=APS Fellow Archive|website=American Physical Society|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1995&unit_id=&institution=University+of+Illinois}} (search on year=1995 and institution=University of Illinois)</ref> and a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (FRS) since 2024.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://royalsociety.org/news/2024/05/new-fellows-2024/ | title=Outstanding scientists elected as Fellows of the Royal Society &#124; Royal Society }}</ref>
